I am now considering a trade with Player 4 for Pennsylvania Avenue, though that would not complete a color group. I am considering offering him cash for properties that would not complete his monopolies, since he has only $433 and could go bankrupt. I also briefly considered trading with Player 1, but no property exchange would help me build a color group.

I will end my turn. I am not trading utilities with Player 1 because a utility pair is too weak to justify giving up Boardwalk. I will not mortgage Boardwalk either, since that would weaken my blocker.

I rejected a multi-step trade with Player 2 because it would still leave me short of the needed properties. I also realized that trading Boardwalk for Player 4's light blue set would give him a dark blue monopoly, which is lethal. I am now considering offering Player 1 all six of their properties in exchange for their entire portfolio.

A full portfolio swap with Player 1 would leave me with incomplete color sets and no monopoly. Player 1 would also receive Boardwalk without completing a dark blue set. I cannot trade for Player 4's Park Place because he needs it to finish his own dark blue set.

I will propose trading $600–$800 cash for Player 4’s Park Place. That would give me a dark blue monopoly and leave me with $358–$558 in cash.

I am calculating the rent and house costs for a dark blue monopoly. Building one house on each property would cost $400, leaving $258 in cash. The rent would rise to $175 on Park Place and $200 on Boardwalk.

I cannot afford to build three houses on both dark blue properties. I would need Park Place for roughly $358 or less, leaving a small cash cushion. Two houses on each property would cost $800 and generate strong rent.

Player 4 will not sell Park Place for $350. I am now considering buying the unowned red properties instead, since they are statistically the best targets on the board. Three reds with houses would cost roughly $680 to acquire plus house construction, which I can afford if I land on them. Trading cannot secure these unowned spaces.

Boardwalk will remain as a permanent block on Player 4. I will end the turn and keep my public message consistent with my previous "Passing" stance.

I will keep my public message focused on buying open reds and oranges, which already blocks Player 1 from completing monopolies. I am now considering a trade with Player 2 to get out of jail, since he has $1300 and owns Marvin Gardens.

I rejected a trade with Player 1 for St. James and New York. Those properties are too weak to justify giving up Electric Company for $400. I also rejected offering Player 4 $400 for Ventnor and Pennsylvania Avenue. That would scatter my holdings across two unrelated color groups and waste cash I need to buy reds.
